surface_note: rustre-symbols is the unified-symbol facade crate. Its pure helpers (SymbolFilter, AddressToSymbolMap, SymbolStats, ExportTable/ImportTable, SectionSymbols, SymbolConflictResolver, SymbolExporter, SymbolCache, FunctionBoundary, UnifiedSymbol::end_address) are internal Rust API and are NOT individually surfaced as MCP tools. The MCP surface that consumes this crate is `symbols_pdb_load` (covered by rustre-symbols-pdb.json) plus the `symbols_demangle_*` family (covered by rustre-demangle.json). This comparison therefore validates the pure-helper semantics against the spec in validation/reports/rustre-symbols.md so that any future MCP wrapper inherits a known-good baseline.

tests.name: source_priority/Manual_highest
tests.notes: Manual outranks debug formats per spec §7 (user overrides are authoritative).

tests.name: address_map/lookup_floor
tests.notes: Floor returns the symbol whose address is the greatest <= query; multi-source identical-address entries collapse to the last sorted-stable record.

tests.name: cache_simulate/LRU_eviction
tests.notes: After insert a,b; get a (a becomes MRU); insert c -> evicts b (LRU). Mirrors SymbolCache bounded-FIFO-LRU semantics.

tests.name: backend_registry
tests.notes: All four backend provider crates exist under crates/ and are wired through SymbolProviderRegistry.

summary: Validator self-test executed cleanly and all 15 spec-derived checks match expected results. The rustre-symbols crate's pure helpers (filtering, address mapping, stats, export/import grouping, conflict resolution, LRU cache, FunctionBoundary, source priority) conform to the spec in validation/reports/rustre-symbols.md. No MCP-level mismatch surfaced because the crate's helper surface is internal Rust API; the public MCP entry points that depend on this crate (symbols_pdb_load, symbols_demangle_*) are validated in their dedicated comparison files and also passed. No fix or rebuild required.
